summary: City of Salamanca steel fire tower erected fall 1938 in Rock City State Forest, Cattaraugus County; derelict and still standing, with the cab apparently gone. Single first-hand account.

facts.design: Steel tower about 40 ft to its floor; maker unidentified (not Aermotor, International Derrick, Blaw-Knox or International Stacey, per the 2022 writer)
facts.status_note: Derelict; the bottom rung of the external ladder is detached, and the 2022 visitor stopped after one step.

access.note: On Rock City State Forest land. The 2022 writer found the tower badly rusted and unsafe to climb.

visit.trail_note: The 2022 writer reached the site by mountain bike and on foot from the Hungry Hollow Road, which was open to the summit ridge that day. State Forest roads open on April 1 or when they dry out.

events.note: Erected by the City of Salamanca in fall 1938 to watch about 1,100 acres of reforested city land around its reservoir; the newspaper account the writer quotes credits the Water & Light Department
The writer believes it was no longer staffed by the time World War II ended; the writer gives no exact date
Visited and described in the April 2022 FFLA-NY newsletter: cab apparently missing, bottom ladder rung detached, steel badly rusted

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The newsletter places the tower in the Town of Little Valley and also says the reservoir it was built to protect is just north of the city. The sources do not contradict each other outright; the story gives both descriptions.

sources.title: New York State Chapter newsletter, April 2022

notes_for_editor: Most of the story rests on one first-hand account in the April 2022 FFLA-NY newsletter. Its staffing and end-of-service statements are the writer's recollection, and the article that named the Elkdale man is lost, so the 1945 end date is approximate. The 1938 build year matches the record. No builder is named by a source; the writer credits the city and the newspaper credits the Water & Light Department. The record's 'north of the city' is kept. The 2022 article's own pictures are not linked. A Facebook group post surfaced in search but was not read. No photo URLs found, so none added.
